about: A Guide entry on Leibniz and the hexagrams in binary order, queued overnight (the user, 2026-10-01: 'please queue up a few more shorts/and ideas'). Same look and voice as guide-wangbi. Draft 2: Astra's revision adopted as is, round 1 (docs/research/2026-10-01-codex-guide-leibniz.md): Leibniz's paper was written in 1703 (printed 1705), the order only attributed to Shao Yong. Line 3 waits 2.2 s so Bouvet's diagram finishes drawing and holds (the user, review board 2026-10-01: 'the yellow diagram when first shown doesn't have enough time to finish displaying').

voice.name: hitchiker's guide v1
voice.note: the user's designed Guide voice ('love it'); plain, even pace, no emphasis announcing the jokes

narration.text: The I-Ching. A book of sixty-four situations, drawn with six solid or broken lines.
narration.picture: THE I-CHING types; an 8×8 grid of small six-line figures.

narration.text: In 1701, missionary Joachim Bouvet sent the mathematician Leibniz a diagram from China.
narration.say: In seventeen-oh-one, missionary Joachim Boo-vay sent the mathematician Leibniz a diagram from China.
narration.picture: An envelope moves from CHINA / 1701 to LEIBNIZ; it opens onto a circle around an 8×8 square.

narration.text: Leibniz already counted using only zeros and ones.
narration.picture: A wig outline beside two columns: 0 1 2 3 4 and 0 1 10 11 100.

narration.text: Here, broken means zero; solid means one. The patterns count from zero to sixty-three.
narration.picture: LEIBNIZ'S READING; four examples, bottom line = leftmost digit: all broken 000000 = 0; top solid 000001 = 1; fifth solid 000010 = 2; all solid 111111 = 63.

narration.text: He was delighted. His paper credited the figures to the legendary Fu Xi.
narration.say: He was delighted. His paper credited the figures to the legendary Foo Shee.
narration.picture: A paper outline: BINARY ARITHMETIC / WRITTEN 1703, then FIGURES: FU XI (LEGEND).

narration.text: The order is attributed to Shao Yong, an eleventh-century scholar.
narration.say: The order is attributed to Shaow Yong, an eleventh-century scholar.
narration.picture: The diagram still; ORDER: ATTRIBUTED TO SHAO YONG / 1011–1077. No crossing out.

narration.text: Recommended for: counting. Not recommended for: checking references.

sources.leibniz: Leibniz, 'Explication de l'Arithmétique Binaire', Mémoires de l'Académie Royale des Sciences, 1703; Bouvet's letter of 4 Nov 1701 with the Xiantian (Earlier Heaven) diagram of Shao Yong (1011-1077). See the Leibniz lesson, series/explainers/leibniz-lesson.json, and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-leibniz-diagram-design.md.
